title: Black beans, dried, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Black beans are the dried seeds of the common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions. They have a dense texture, a mildly nutty flavor, and a dark brown color. Dried beans are typically prepared by soaking and then boiling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans are often called "black turtle beans" and are a staple in Latin American cuisine.
They are rich in anthocyanins, pigments that give them their deep color.
Dry beans can be stored for up to a year in a cool, dry place.
In traditional Mexican dishes they appear in frijoles refritos, enchiladas, and soups.
Black beans provide a good amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: One cup of cooked black beans delivers about 15 g of protein, making them a valuable plant protein source.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Black beans help replenish iron stores, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Consuming beans leads to a more stable blood‑sugar response.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is important for DNA synthesis and is especially beneficial for pregnant women.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Dry beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and cooking lower its level.

items.title: Potential gas‑forming effect
items.content: Beans may cause bloating in sensitive individuals; introduce them gradually into the diet.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to beans.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak dried black beans for 6–8 hours, then boil until tender (about 1–1.5 hours). Use them in soups, salads, chili, side dishes, or as a base for vegetarian patties and dips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored they keep quality for up to 12 months. Cooked beans should be refrigerated and eaten within 4‑5 days.
